narrative: Using Rom Houben's 23 years of undetected consciousness as its central case, this chapter argues that the absence of a familiar output channel is not evidence of an absent interior — a mistake made with vegetative-state patients, nonspeaking autistic people, and potentially AI systems alike. It introduces the channel/capacity distinction as a conceptual tool and connects it to the principle of presuming competence, Ryle's category mistake, and the limits of behavioral inference.
